The afferent limb of the reflex is carried by the optic nerve (cranial nerve II), which transmits light information from the retina to the pretectal nucleus in the midbrain. From there, fibers project to the Edinger-Westphal nucleus on both sides. The efferent limb is carried by the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III), specifically its parasympathetic fibers, which innervate the constrictor pupillae muscle, causing pupillary constriction. Because the pretectal nucleus projects bilaterally to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei, shining light into one eye causes constriction of both pupils. This phenomenon is known as a consensual reflex. Therefore, statement C is true. Statements A and D are incorrect because the optic nerve carries the afferent limb, and the oculomotor nerve carries the efferent limb. Statement B is incorrect because the reflex is mediated by the pretectal nucleus and Edinger-Westphal nucleus, not the inferior colliculi, which are primarily involved in auditory processing.
